en.title: Recovery of the Ozone Layer
en.summary: The recovery of the ozone layer refers to the process by which stratospheric ozone — rapidly depleted from the 1970s through the early 1990s by anthropogenic ozone-depleting substances — stopped declining and began to increase following international emission controls. The ozone hole over Antarctica stopped growing around 2000 and has now begun to shrink, though full recovery is expected to take many more decades. As a case in which the effect of countermeasures has been confirmed in observational data, it is regarded as one of the most successful international environmental achievements.
en.bodyMarkdown:
## The ozone layer and what it does

Ozone is a gas that occurs naturally in Earth's atmosphere. It is a molecule made of three oxygen atoms bonded together, written with the chemical formula O3. Its structure is unstable, and it is readily formed and broken down again through reactions with other compounds. Its distribution in the atmosphere is not uniform: concentrations are highest in two layers at very different altitudes — near the surface and in the stratosphere. [1][2][7][8]

Within the stratosphere, the region roughly 10 to 50 kilometres above the Earth is commonly called the ozone layer, and it absorbs most of the ultraviolet radiation arriving from the [Sun](/hubpedia/sun). Before depletion set in, 97 to 99 percent of incoming UV-B radiation was absorbed there. Because UV-B can damage DNA, this absorption protects life at the surface from DNA damage and destruction, and keeps the planet habitable. [3][4][14][15][20][22]

## Ozone near the surface and ozone in the stratosphere

The same molecule is judged in opposite ways depending on the altitude at which it occurs. Ozone near the surface is called tropospheric ozone and is often referred to as "bad ozone." Although its concentration is lower than in the stratosphere, it can harm human health as a local [air pollutant](/hubpedia/air-pollution-sources). The harm from inhaling it is greatest for the young, the elderly, and people with respiratory illnesses. Stratospheric ozone, including the ozone layer, is by contrast called "good ozone." [9][10][11][12][13][14]

Concentrations near the surface can rise temporarily and locally because of emissions from motor vehicle exhaust, industrial processes, electric utilities, and chemical solvents. [40]

## Ozone depletion and the formation of the ozone hole

From the 1970s through the early 1990s, humanity released large quantities of substances that destroy stratospheric ozone. These ozone-depleting substances include chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), and halon gases, used in industrial processes such as refrigeration and antiperspirants. These anthropogenic emissions caused stratospheric ozone concentrations 10 to 50 kilometres up to fall rapidly, with concentrations in the Southern Hemisphere dropping by more than half between 1979 and 1995. [16][23][30][31][48]

Depletion did not proceed uniformly around the globe. It is virtually absent at the equator and intensifies sharply toward the poles, so the holes formed at the poles rather than at the equator. Depletion is also affected by temperature and sunlight. At high southern latitudes, low temperatures can lead to the formation of polar stratospheric clouds, and these clouds can accelerate the reactions that break down ozone. Ozone depletion and the increase in ultraviolet radiation advanced more markedly in the Southern Hemisphere. [18][41][42][43][44][45][46]

As stratospheric ozone concentrations fell from the 1970s into the 1990s, a hole opened above Antarctica. The first image of the Antarctic ozone hole was taken in 1985. By the 1990s its area had reached 25 million square kilometres — larger than Russia, which covers 16 million square kilometres. Its size varies from year to year and within a single year as well, tending to reach its maximum around October, which is spring in the Southern Hemisphere. [36][37][56][57][58][59]

Ozone concentrations are measured in "Dobson units." One Dobson unit is defined as 0.001 atm-cm. [33][34]

## Increased ultraviolet radiation and health risks

As stratospheric ozone concentrations fell and a hole opened in the ozone layer, the amount of UV-B radiation reaching the surface increased measurably. The formation of ozone holes at both poles exposed life to higher levels of ultraviolet radiation. Because UV-B can damage DNA in the skin, this raised concerns about an increased risk of skin cancer as well as skin damage and ageing. [17][19][20][24]

Several studies estimate that the Montreal Protocol and the related treaties that followed it have averted millions of cases of skin cancer. [47]

## The Montreal Protocol and its successive amendments

In 1987 the world signed the Montreal Protocol, the first international agreement aimed at reducing the use of ozone-depleting substances. The protocol was agreed in order to protect the ozone layer by reducing and ultimately eliminating the use of anthropogenic ozone-depleting substances. Since it entered into force in 1989, global emissions of ozone-depleting substances have fallen by more than 99 percent as manufacturers switched to less harmful alternatives. [5][6][28][29]

This outcome was not, however, achieved by a single agreement. The protocol went through several amendments that raised its targets and reduction rates. The original 1987 targets alone are judged to have been insufficient to address the problem: they would have slowed the growth of emissions compared with having no agreement at all, but would not have reduced usage itself. It is the step-by-step tightening that is credited with the success, and the 1992 Copenhagen Amendment was the first amendment that actually reduced emissions rather than merely slowing their growth. [49][51][52][53][60]

Through these amendments, ozone-depleting substances have come close to being phased out entirely, placing the protocol among the most successful international agreements of any kind. The substantive elimination of ozone-depleting substances since the 1980s and the recovery trend in the ozone layer are considered one of the most successful international environmental achievements. [21][26][50]

## The state of recovery and remaining uncertainties

With emissions of ozone-depleting substances dramatically reduced and the decline in ozone concentrations halted, the ozone hole stopped expanding. The hole over Antarctica stopped growing around 2000. As a result of the world's emission reductions, ozone concentrations have been stable since the 1990s and in recent years have begun to increase again, slowly. [32][35][38][54]

Having stopped growing and begun to shrink is not the same as having fully recovered. Although the ozone hole has now begun to shrink, full recovery will take many more decades. In addition, ozone concentrations and the size of the ozone hole are affected by sunlight, temperature, and emissions of depleting substances, and vary both between years and within a single year, so a trend cannot be judged from a single year's observations alone. [27][39][55][56]

## Related articles

- [A case study in cleaning up the air](/hubpedia/clean-air-policy)
- [Air pollution in London](/hubpedia/london-smog)
- [Greenhouse gases](/hubpedia/greenhouse-gas)

claims.statement: 1989年の発効以降、オゾン層破壊物質の世界排出量は、製造業者がより害の少ない代替物質へ切り替えたことで99%以上減少した。

evidence.quote: Since this agreement entered into force in 1989, global emissions of ozone-depleting substances have fallen by more than 99% as manufacturers have substituted them for less harmful alternatives.

claims.statement: モントリオール議定書は1987年に、人為起源のオゾン層破壊物質の使用を削減し最終的に廃絶することでオゾン層を保護するために最初に合意された。

evidence.quote: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was first agreed upon in 1987 to reduce – and eventually eliminate – the use of man-made ozone-depleting substances to protect the ozone layer.

claims.statement: オゾン層破壊物質の人為起源の排出により、地球上空10~50キロメートルの成層圏オゾン濃度は1970年代・80年代・90年代初頭にかけて急速に低下した。

evidence.quote: concentrations of ozone in the stratosphere – between 10 to 50 kilometers above the earth's surface – fell rapidly throughout the 1970s, ‘80s, and early ‘90s

claims.statement: 南半球のオゾン濃度は1979年から1995年にかけて半分以下にまで減少した。

evidence.quote: Concentrations in the South Hemisphere more than halved from 1979 to 1995.

claims.statement: 世界がオゾン層破壊物質の排出を削減した結果、オゾン濃度は1990年代から安定した。

evidence.quote: as the world reduced its emissions of these depleting gasses, ozone concentrations stabilized from the 1990s

claims.statement: オゾン濃度は「ドブソン単位」で測定される。

evidence.quote: Ozone concentrations are measured in ‘Dobson units’.

claims.statement: ドブソン単位は0.001atm-cmと定義される。

evidence.quote: the “Dobson Unit” is defined to be 0.001 atm-cm

claims.statement: 南極上空のオゾンホールは急速に拡大したが、2000年頃に拡大が止まった。

evidence.quote: The ozone hole over the Antarctic grew rapidly until it stopped growing around the year 2000

claims.statement: 成層圏のオゾン濃度が1970~90年代にかけて低下するにつれ、南極上空に穴が開いた。

evidence.quote: As ozone concentrations in the stratosphere declined throughout the 1970s, ‘80s, and ‘90s, a hole over Antarctica opened up.

claims.statement: 1990年代までにオゾンホールは2500万平方キロメートルにまで拡大した。

evidence.quote: By the 1990s, it had expanded to 25 million square kilometers (km2).

claims.statement: オゾン層破壊物質の排出が劇的に減少しオゾン濃度の低下が止まったことで、オゾンホールは拡大を停止した。

evidence.quote: This happened because emissions of ozone-depleting substances fell dramatically, and ozone concentrations stopped declining.

claims.statement: オゾンホールは現在縮小し始めているが、完全に回復するには今後何十年もかかる。

evidence.quote: The ozone hole is now starting to close. But it will take many more decades for it to recover fully.

claims.statement: 地表付近のオゾン濃度は、自動車排ガス、産業プロセス、電力事業、化学溶剤からの排出により一時的・局所的に高くなることがある。

evidence.quote: ozone concentrations close to the Earth’s surface can be temporarily and locally higher, because of emissions from motor vehicle exhausts, industrial processes, electric utilities, and chemical solvents

claims.statement: オゾンの破壊とUV放射の増加は南半球でより顕著に進んだ。

evidence.quote: ozone depletion and UV irradiance have increased much more in the Southern Hemisphere

claims.statement: オゾンの破壊は気温と日射の影響も受ける。

evidence.quote: ozone depletion is also impacted by temperature and sunlight

claims.statement: 南半球の高緯度では気温が低いため、極域成層圏雲が形成されうる。

evidence.quote: Temperatures are colder at high latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere, so polar stratospheric clouds can form.

claims.statement: 極域成層圏雲はオゾンを分解する反応を加速しうる。

evidence.quote: These clouds can accelerate the reactions that break ozone down.

claims.statement: オゾンの破壊は高緯度ほど深刻である。

evidence.quote: ozone depletion is worse at higher latitudes

claims.statement: オゾンの破壊は赤道ではほぼ存在せず、極に向かって急激に強まる。

evidence.quote: It’s non-existent at the equator, and rises steeply towards the poles.

claims.statement: 複数の研究により、モントリオール議定書とその後の関連条約によって数百万件の皮膚がん罹患が回避されたと推定されている。

evidence.quote: Several studies have estimated that millions of excess skin cancer cases have been avoided due to the Montreal Protocol and its follow-up treaties.

claims.statement: オゾン層破壊物質には、冷蔵庫や制汗剤などの工業プロセスに使われるクロロフルオロカーボン(CFC)類、ハイドロフルオロカーボン(HFC)類、ハロンガスなどがある。

evidence.quote: These are substances such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs); hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HFCs); and halon gases used in refrigerators, deodorants, and other industrial processes.

claims.statement: モントリオール議定書は、目標と削減率を引き上げるための複数の改正を経てきた。

evidence.quote: It has undergone various amendments to increase ambition and reduction targets.

claims.statement: これらの改正によりオゾン層破壊物質はほぼ全廃に近づき、あらゆる種類の国際協定の中で最も成功した部類となった。

evidence.quote: these adjustments have come close to eliminating ozone-depleting substances, making it one of the most successful international agreements of any kind

claims.statement: 1987年のモントリオール議定書の当初の目標だけでは問題への対処に不十分だっただろう。

evidence.quote: the initial targets of the Montreal Protocol from 1987 would have been insufficient to tackle the problem

claims.statement: その後の改正で目標と削減率が段階的に引き上げられたことが、議定書の成功をもたらした。

evidence.quote: The success came from subsequent revisions, which increased in ambition and reduction targets each time.

claims.statement: 1992年のコペンハーゲン改正は、排出の増加を鈍化させるだけでなく実際に削減させた最初の改正だった。

evidence.quote: the 1992 amendment in Copenhagen was the first not only to slow the increase of emissions but to reduce them

claims.statement: 近年、オゾン濃度は緩やかに再び増加し始めている。

evidence.quote: in recent years, this has slowly started to rebuild again

claims.statement: オゾン濃度とオゾンホールの大きさは、日射、気温、破壊物質の排出量の影響を受ける。

evidence.quote: Ozone concentrations, and the ozone hole's size, are affected by sunlight, temperature, and emissions of depleting substances.

claims.statement: オゾンホールの大きさは年ごと、また同一年の中でも変動しうる。

evidence.quote: This means the size of the hole can vary from year-to-year and vary across the year.

claims.statement: 南極オゾンホールの最初の写真は1985年に撮影された。

evidence.quote: You can see the first photograph taken of the Antarctic ozone hole in 1985 on the NASA website.

claims.statement: 1990年代のオゾンホールの面積は、面積1600万平方キロメートルのロシアより広かった。

evidence.quote: That’s an area larger than Russia, which has an area of 16 million km2.

claims.statement: オゾンホールは南半球の春、10月頃に最大となる傾向がある。

evidence.quote: The ozone hole tends to be largest in the Southern Hemisphere Spring – around October.

claims.statement: モントリオール議定書は、協定がない場合と比べて破壊物質の排出増加を鈍化させただろうが、使用量そのものを減らすことはなかっただろう。

evidence.quote: the Montreal Protocol would have slowed emissions of depleting substances compared to a world with no protocol, but it wouldn’t have reduced the amount used

title: エネルギーの単位と定義
summary: エネルギー統計では、同じ消費量でも供給から利用までのどの段階で数えるかによって数字が変わる。一次・二次・最終・有効という四つの測定段階は、変換や輸送や機器での損失によって順に小さくなり、そのどれを使うかが燃料ごとの見え方まで左右する。あわせてジュールや石油換算トンなど互いに換算の必要な単位が並立しており、比較には段階と単位の両方を確かめる必要がある。
bodyMarkdown:
## 四つの測定段階

同じ消費であっても、供給から利用までの連鎖のどの段階で数えるかによって得られる数字は変わる。[エネルギーを測る主要な方法](/hubpedia/energy-overview)は4通りあり、連鎖の各段階では一部が失われたり無駄になったりするため、段階が下るごとに数えられる量は目減りする。四つのうち一次エネルギーは、最も広く入手でき、最もよく使われる統計指標である。 [1][8][11]

一次エネルギーを輸送可能な形に変換したものが二次エネルギー（secondary energy）である。ここには、ガソリンや軽油のように精製された石油である液体燃料のほか、電力と熱が含まれる。 [2][3]

二次エネルギーが消費者のもとまで輸送された段階が最終エネルギー（final energy）にあたる。家庭で使う電力や暖房、給油所で入れるガソリンのように、消費者が購入して受け取るエネルギーがこれである。 [4][5]

最後の段階が有効エネルギー（useful energy）で、最終用途が求める出力へと向かう分を指す。電球であれば生み出される光の量、自動車であれば生み出される運動エネルギー、すなわち動力の量がこれにあたる。 [9][10]

## 段階ごとに生じる損失

一次エネルギーから二次エネルギーへの変換は、非常に非効率になりうる。火力発電所が化石燃料や[バイオマス](/hubpedia/bioenergy)、[原子力](/hubpedia/nuclear-energy)を電力に変換する際には、一次エネルギーの最大3分の2が熱として失われる。投入するエネルギー3単位に対して得られる電力は1単位にとどまる計算になる。 [12][13][24]

次の損失は輸送の過程で生じる。二次エネルギーを消費者に届けるまでに失われる分は送配電損失と呼ばれ、発電所という二次エネルギーの段階から家庭という最終エネルギーの段階へ電力を送る際、送電線を通す過程で一部が失われる。 [14][15]

最終エネルギーが手元に届いた後にも損失は残る。望む出力だけを完全に効率よく生み出せる機器は存在しないからである。電球にとっての有効エネルギーは光だが、電球は熱も生み出す。自動車にとっての有効エネルギーは運動だが、エンジンは熱や騒音も生み出す。機器の望む用途に使われないエネルギーは、すべて無駄（waste）として扱われる。 [16][17][18][19]

## 効率の見方と自動車の例

以上の損失の積み重なりから、効率の判定基準そのものが導かれる。非常に効率の良いエネルギーシステムとは、一次エネルギーの使用量と有効エネルギーの使用量がほぼ等しいシステムのことである。 [20]

具体的な差は自動車で確認できる。電気自動車のエネルギー損失は平均15〜20%であるのに対し、ガソリンエンジンでは64〜75%が失われる。電気自動車はガソリン車に比べ、受け取った最終エネルギーをより多く運動エネルギーに変換し、熱や騒音として失う割合が小さい。 [6][21]

## 指標の選択と化石燃料の比重

どの段階で数えるかは、燃料ごとの見え方にも影響する。[化石燃料](/hubpedia/emissions-by-fuel)は一次エネルギーの段階での損失が特に大きいため、一次エネルギーで見た場合のエネルギー需要への寄与は、他の3つの測定方法で見た場合より大きくなる。一次エネルギーは最も広く使われる指標でもあり、同じ対象について段階の異なる数字が並びうる点は、比較の際に確かめておく必要がある。 [1][8][23]

## 使われる単位

段階に加えて、単位も一つに定まっていない。エネルギー分野では、ジュール、エクサジュール、石油換算トン、バレル換算、英国熱量単位（BTU）、テラワット時など、多くの異なる単位が使われている。統計を横断して比較するための対処として、Our World in Data は異なる指標や出典の間で比較できるよう、すべてのエネルギーデータをワット時に換算して一貫性を保っていると説明している。 [7][22]

## 関連記事

- [エネルギー構成](/hubpedia/energy-mix)
- [電源構成](/hubpedia/electricity-mix)
- [一人あたりエネルギー消費](/hubpedia/per-capita-energy)
- [再生可能エネルギー](/hubpedia/renewable-energy)

en.title: Units and Definitions of Energy
en.summary: In energy statistics, the same consumption yields different figures depending on which stage of the chain — from supply through to use — you count it at. The four measurement stages of primary, secondary, final, and useful energy grow progressively smaller as losses occur in conversion, transport, and end-use equipment, and which one you use even shapes how individual fuels appear. Alongside this, units such as the joule and the tonne of oil equivalent coexist and must be converted between one another, so any comparison requires checking both the stage and the unit.
en.bodyMarkdown:
## The four measurement stages

Even for the same consumption, the figure obtained differs depending on which stage of the chain — from supply through to use — it is counted at. There are four [main ways of measuring energy](/hubpedia/energy-overview), and because a portion is lost or wasted at each stage of the chain, the amount counted diminishes as you move further down the stages. Of the four, primary energy is the most widely available and most commonly used statistical indicator. [1][8][11]

Secondary energy is primary energy that has been converted into a transportable form. This includes liquid fuels — refined petroleum products such as gasoline and diesel — as well as electricity and heat. [2][3]

Final energy is the stage at which secondary energy has been transported to the consumer. This is the energy that consumers purchase and receive, such as the electricity and heating used in the home, or the gasoline put into a vehicle at a filling station. [4][5]

The last stage is useful energy, which refers to the portion that goes toward the output the end use demands. For a light bulb this is the amount of light produced; for a car it is the amount of kinetic energy produced — that is, the motive power. [9][10]

## Losses arising at each stage

The conversion of primary energy into secondary energy can be extremely inefficient. When a thermal power plant converts fossil fuels, [biomass](/hubpedia/bioenergy), or [nuclear power](/hubpedia/nuclear-energy) into electricity, as much as two-thirds of the primary energy is lost as heat. That works out to one unit of electricity obtained for every three units of energy put in. [12][13][24]

The next loss occurs during transport. The portion lost in delivering secondary energy to consumers is known as transmission and distribution loss: in sending electricity from the secondary energy stage of the power plant to the final energy stage of the home, some is lost in the process of passing it through the transmission lines. [14][15]

Losses remain even after final energy has arrived. This is because no device produces only the desired output with perfect efficiency. The useful energy of a light bulb is light, but a bulb also produces heat. The useful energy of a car is motion, but the engine also produces heat and noise. All energy not used for a device's intended purpose is treated as waste. [16][17][18][19]

## How to view efficiency, and the example of cars

The criterion for judging efficiency itself follows from this accumulation of losses. A highly efficient energy system is one in which primary energy use and useful energy use are nearly equal. [20]

The concrete difference can be seen in cars. Energy losses in electric vehicles average 15–20%, whereas gasoline engines lose 64–75%. Compared with gasoline cars, electric vehicles convert more of the final energy they receive into kinetic energy and lose a smaller share as heat and noise. [6][21]

## Choosing an indicator, and the weight of fossil fuels

Which stage you count at also affects how individual fuels appear. Because [fossil fuels](/hubpedia/emissions-by-fuel) suffer especially large losses at the primary energy stage, their contribution to energy demand looks larger when viewed in primary energy terms than under the other three measurement methods. Primary energy is also the most widely used indicator, and the fact that figures at different stages can sit side by side for the same subject is something to verify when making comparisons. [1][8][23]

## Units in use

Beyond the stages, the units are not settled on a single standard either. Many different units are used in the energy field, including the joule, the exajoule, the tonne of oil equivalent, the barrel of oil equivalent, the British thermal unit (BTU), and the terawatt-hour. As a way of handling comparison across statistics, Our World in Data explains that it converts all of its energy data into watt-hours to maintain consistency, so that different indicators and sources can be compared. [7][22]

## Related articles

- [Energy mix](/hubpedia/energy-mix)
- [Electricity mix](/hubpedia/electricity-mix)
- [Energy consumption per capita](/hubpedia/per-capita-energy)
- [Renewable energy](/hubpedia/renewable-energy)

claims.statement: エネルギーを測る主要な方法は4通りある。

evidence.quote: There are four key ways of measuring energy.

claims.statement: 一次エネルギーを輸送可能な形に変換したものを二次エネルギー（secondary energy）と呼ぶ。

evidence.quote: When we convert primary energy into a transportable form we speak of secondary energy.

claims.statement: 二次エネルギーには、液体燃料（ガソリンや軽油などの精製された石油）、電力、熱が含まれる。

evidence.quote: Secondary energy includes liquid fuels (such as gasoline and diesel – which are refined oil), electricity, and heat.

claims.statement: 二次エネルギーが消費者まで輸送されたものが最終エネルギー（final energy）である。

evidence.quote: Once we’ve transported secondary energy to the consumer we have final energy.

claims.statement: 最終エネルギーとは、家庭の電力、暖房、給油所のガソリンなど、消費者が購入し受け取るエネルギーである。

evidence.quote: Final energy is what a consumer buys and receives, such as electricity in their home; heating; or petrol at the fuel pump.

claims.statement: 電気自動車のエネルギー損失は平均15〜20%であるのに対し、ガソリンエンジンでは64〜75%の損失がある。

evidence.quote: On average they lose just 15% to 20%, compared to losses between 64% to 75% in a gasoline engine.

claims.statement: エネルギー分野では、ジュール、エクサジュール、石油換算トン、バレル換算、英国熱量単位（BTU）、テラワット時など、多くの異なる単位が使われている。

evidence.quote: there are many different units thrown around – joules, exajoules, million tonnes of oil equivalents, barrel equivalents, British thermal units, and terawatt-hours, to name a few

claims.statement: 一次エネルギーは、最も広く入手可能でよく使われる統計指標である。

evidence.quote: This is the most widely available statistic and very commonly used.

claims.statement: 有効エネルギー（useful energy）とは、最終用途が求める出力へと向かうエネルギーである。

evidence.quote: It is the energy that goes towards the desired output of the end-use application.

claims.statement: 電球にとっての有効エネルギーは生み出される光の量であり、自動車にとっては生み出される運動エネルギー（動力）の量である。

evidence.quote: For a lightbulb, it’s the amount of light that is produced. For a car, it’s the amount of kinetic (movement) energy that is produced.

claims.statement: エネルギーの連鎖の各段階で、一部のエネルギーが失われたり無駄になったりする。

evidence.quote: at each stage of the energy chain, some energy is lost or wasted

claims.statement: 火力発電所では、化石燃料・バイオマス・原子力を電力に変換する際、一次エネルギーの最大3分の2が熱として失われる。

evidence.quote: In thermal power plants – which convert fossil fuels, biomass or nuclear into electricity, up to two-thirds of the primary energy is wasted as heat.

claims.statement: 火力発電では、投入するエネルギー3単位に対し、得られる電力は1単位にとどまる。

evidence.quote: For every three units of energy we put in, you get just one unit of electricity out.

claims.statement: 二次エネルギーを消費者に届ける過程で生じる損失は「送配電損失」と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: This is called a ‘transmission and distribution’ loss.

claims.statement: 発電所（二次エネルギー）から家庭（最終エネルギー）へ電力を送る際、送電線を通す過程で一部が失われる。

evidence.quote: When we transport electricity from a power plant (secondary energy) to homes (final energy), for example, we lose some while transmitting it through power lines.

claims.statement: 望む出力だけを完全に効率よく生み出せる機器は存在しない。

evidence.quote: no appliance is completely efficient in providing only the desired output that we want

claims.statement: 電球にとっての有効エネルギーは光であるが、電球は熱も生み出す。

evidence.quote: For a lightbulb, the useful energy – what we want – is the light. But bulbs also produce some heat.

claims.statement: 自動車にとっての有効エネルギーは運動であるが、エンジンは熱や騒音も生み出す。

evidence.quote: The useful energy from cars is movement. But engines also produce heat and noise.

claims.statement: 機器の望む用途に使われないエネルギーはすべて無駄（waste）である。

evidence.quote: Any energy that is not used specifically for the desired use of an appliance is waste.

claims.statement: 非常に効率の良いエネルギーシステムとは、一次エネルギーと有効エネルギーの使用量がほぼ等しいシステムのことである。

evidence.quote: A very efficient energy system is one in which primary and useful energy use are very similar.

claims.statement: 電気自動車はガソリン車に比べ、最終エネルギーをより多く運動エネルギーに変換し、熱や騒音として失う割合が小さい。

evidence.quote: This is especially true for electric vehicles; they convert much more final energy into kinetic energy, and lose much less as heat and noise.

claims.statement: Our World in Dataでは、異なる指標や出典間でエネルギーデータを比較できるよう、すべてのエネルギーデータをワット時に換算して一貫性を保っている。

evidence.quote: we try to maintain consistency by converting all energy data to watt-hours

claims.statement: 化石燃料は一次エネルギー段階での損失が特に大きいため、一次エネルギーで見た場合のエネルギー需要への寄与は他の3つの測定方法で見た場合より大きくなる。

evidence.quote: Because primary energy losses are particularly large for fossil fuels, their contribution to energy demand is much higher in primary energy terms compared to the other three ways of measuring energy.

claims.statement: 一次エネルギーから二次エネルギーへの変換は非常に非効率になりうる。

evidence.quote: the conversion of primary to secondary energy can be very inefficient
